question: What will the Antarctic sea ice extent be on September 21, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Antarctic sea ice extent for 2026-09-21 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
# Antarctic sea ice extent on 2026-09-21 (NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4): research brief

On 2026-08-16 the Antarctic extent was 16.288 million km². That is about 0.2 million km² below 2024 and 2025 on the same date, and only 2023 was lower among the years I checked. In the past seven seasons, extent grew 0.65 to 1.21 million km² between Aug 16 and Sep 21. Adding that range to 16.288 gives about 16.94 to 17.50 million km², centred near 17.26. Nothing settles the question yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding file is NSIDC's [S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv). Each daily value is normally posted about a day later, so as of 2026-08-17 the latest value is probably 2026-08-16.
- Daily values in that file, in million km²:
  - 2026-08-01: 16.222
  - 2026-08-04: 16.369, a local peak
  - 2026-08-08: 16.292
  - 2026-08-11: 15.955, a dip
  - 2026-08-13: 16.030
  - 2026-08-15: 16.170
  - 2026-08-16: 16.288
- The mid-August dip took about 0.41 million km² off between Aug 4 and Aug 11. Extent then recovered at roughly 0.06 to 0.12 million km² per day.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. The annual maximum usually comes in mid to late September, so Sep 21 is usually at or close to the peak.
- 2026 is running below most recent years on the same date (table in section 4).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-03: Met Office briefing:
  - It gives Antarctic extent as 16.65 million km² on Aug 2, 0.83 below the 1981-2010 average. The summary calls this 5th lowest for the date, but the body text says 4th lowest.
  - That figure is higher than NSIDC's 16.212 for Aug 2, so the Met Office is probably using a different dataset.
  - July averaged 15.39 million km², the 5th lowest July on record.
  - Ice grew about 76,000 km² per day, slightly faster than the 72,000 average.
  - Ice was below average from the Weddell Sea through the Indian Ocean sector.
  - Drivers named were a strongly positive Southern Annular Mode and a developing El Niño.
  - [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- Zack Labe's tracker page reportedly has a graphic for monitoring record-low extent. I did not check what it shows. [zacklabe.com](https://zacklabe.com/antarctic-sea-ice-extentconcentration/)
- I could not find an NSIDC "Sea Ice Today" post on Antarctic conditions published in August 2026 before the 17th.

## 4. Base rates
All values are NSIDC v4, in million km², read from the same CSV:

| Year | Aug 16 | Sep 21 | Change | Annual max (date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 17.365 | 18.174 | +0.81 | n/a |
| 2019 | 17.570 | 18.252 | +0.68 | 18.489 (Sep 26) |
| 2020 | 17.753 | 18.836 | +1.08 | 19.062 (Sep 25) |
| 2021 | n/a | about 18.2 (approximate) | n/a | about 18.9 (late Aug) |
| 2022 | 17.021 | 18.222 | +1.20 | 18.276 (Sep 13) |
| 2023 | 15.644 | 16.832 | +1.19 | 17.109 (Sep 7) |
| 2024 | 16.557 | 17.211 | +0.65 | about 17.28 (Sep 15) |
| 2025 | 16.492 | 17.702 | +1.21 | 17.854 (Sep 15) |

- **Growth from Aug 16 to Sep 21:** the average is about +0.97 and the range is +0.65 to +1.21 (spread about 0.56).
- **Applied to 2026:** adding that range to 16.288 gives about 16.94 to 17.50, centred near 17.26.
- **Trend:** Sep 21 values were around 18.2 to 18.8 in 2018-2022. Since 2023 they have been much lower, at 16.8 to 17.7.
- **Day-to-day noise:** daily values in late September can move 0.1 to 0.3 within a few days, so Sep 21 may fall a little before or after the peak.
- **Data caveats:**
  - The 2021 values are approximate because I could only read a summary for that part of the file.
  - The 2024 maximum comes from a partial view of that year.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question.
- I found no expert forecast of the September 21 extent. The Met Office and NSIDC publish monitoring reports, not point forecasts for Antarctic extent.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Daily NSIDC updates:** one value per day through 2026-09-21. The resolving value should appear around Sep 22, but values for the most recent days can be revised slightly.
- **Weather:** synoptic storms can cause swings like the Aug 4-11 drop, and a strongly positive Southern Annular Mode is in place. Watch the Weddell Sea and Indian Ocean sectors, where ice was below average.
- **Expected reports:**
  - A Met Office September briefing in early September.
  - An NSIDC "Sea Ice Today" analysis in early September.
  - A Copernicus August summary in early September.
  - An NSIDC announcement of the Antarctic maximum in late September, probably after the question resolves.

Sources:
- [NSIDC S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- [Met Office August 2026 briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
